version.changelog: v3: 容量管理/FTS5索引/跨会话召回/用户图谱/自动Skill创建

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions mostly match a local file-based memory manager, but there are undeclared LLM/data-exchange dependencies and file-write behaviors that deserve review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (multi-partition memory, consolidation, FTS5 + LLM summaries, auto skill generation) align with the included scripts (context loaders, consolidate, capacity manager, conflict detector, user_model, skill-creator). However SKILL.md and scripts reference LLM summarization and automatic skill generation which typically require network/API credentials and broader capabilities not declared in the registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate on a local memory directory (read/write/move/create files under MEMORY_DIR). They create state files (.auto_loader_state.json, .capacity_state.json, .restore_log.json, memory/.user_graph.json, archive/index.json, etc.), and auto_skill_generator can write new skill artifacts. The SKILL.md instructs loading and injecting recall into prompts and invoking LLM summarizers. The instructions do not explicitly document any external network calls, but code imports an LLMSummarizer (from fts5_index) implying external LLM usage; no LLM env vars are declared. The skill will read many markdown files under the memory workspace but does not ask to access other system files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + shipped scripts). That lowers supply-chain risk because nothing is automatically downloaded, but the package does include many executable Python files that will run locally when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code uses OPENCLAW_MEMORY_DIR (default /root/.openclaw/workspace/memory) but the skill declares no required env vars or credentials. The SKILL.md and code reference LLM-based summarization (LLMSummarizer) which commonly requires API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar) — these credentials are not declared. This is an inconsistency: either the summarizer is purely local (not shown) or it will require secret credentials that the skill didn't request/explain.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and model invocation allowed (defaults). The skill writes state and index files into the memory workspace and can generate new skill files via the skill-creator module. Writing its own state and archive files is expected for this functionality, but automatic skill generation increases the blast radius (it can create new code artifacts in the workspace). There is no evidence it modifies other skills' configs, but review is advised.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing:

- Review fts5_index.py and session_search.py (the LLMSummarizer implementation). Confirm whether they call external LLM APIs and which environment variables or keys are required; the registry metadata currently lists no required credentials.
- Note the default memory directory is /root/.openclaw/workspace/memory. If you install, either set OPENCLAW_MEMORY_DIR to a safe sandbox path or inspect/backup that directory — scripts will read, move, write, and delete files under it (archive moves, consolidation, state files, index files).
- The skill can auto-generate new skills (scripts/skill-creator/). If you want to avoid code generation, audit or disable the auto_skill_generator module before use.
- Run the code in a restricted/sandboxed environment first (non-root account, isolated workspace) so you can observe network activity and files created. Monitor outbound network calls during a dry-run to confirm no unexpected endpoints are contacted.
- If you plan to enable LLM summaries, supply API keys only after verifying the summarizer’s provider and adding least-privilege controls; prefer providing keys via short-lived or scoped creds and not embedding them in global configs.

Reason for suspicion: the package claims LLM-driven features but does not declare any required credentials and includes modules that create and write code artifacts — both are valid behaviors for the feature set but are undeclared and widen the scope of what will run on your machine. Review those specific files and run in a sandbox before trusting it with production data.
